strings.ANT_Tourist_Wasteland_desc:
While Antigua has always been reliant on foreign powers for trade, at least in the past its economy relied on two pillars. By the time the bells of indepence ushered a new epoch, however, one of the had long since turned to dust. Without irrigation, infrastructure, or consolidation, there are almost no staple crops being produced in the area, making the local economy and the lives of the island's inhabitants totally dependent on foreign aid.

The one saving grace for Antigua is its tourist industry, which, while still outcompeted by most other Caribbean nations, provides the necessary income to keep at least a portion of the island's population affluent.
strings.ANT_Magpie_Treasure_desc: Corruption is rampant within Antigua and it is by no means a secret. Vere Bird has been in charge of the island for decades, with his family numbering among the island's richest inhabitants, joined by by the new class of elites that filled the thrones left desolate following the collapse of the plantations. Union men and administrators, loyal only to the dollar, and only as long as it lines their pockets. Bird may be the face and champion of this status quo, but he is by no means the sole claimant to it.
strings.ANT_Reign_Rooster_desc:
Vere Bird, the strongman Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda, has ruled the nation with an iron fist since his days as a union boss during the war. He and his family lord over the island like a feudal dynasty, using his dual control over both the Antigua Trade and Labour Union and the Antigua Labour Party to dominate the country's political scene.

This status quo has only been slightly shaken with the coming of independence and the belated rise of a rival party, the Progressive Labour Movement. However, tossing the old Bird from his roost will be no small feat.
strings.ANT_Northern_Migration_desc:
George Walter has achieved the impossible in unseating Vere Bird, and in a bitter tragedy must now achieve it once more. Following his defeat, Bird has fled to New York, and he was by no means the sole one to do so. With a significant portion of the state apparatus in chaos and the country's reserves sacked, Walter has found Vere's absence to be just as worse.

Though tears may be shed now, the tragedy may yet worsen and transform into a farce. After all, if he fails to rebuild the country, what's to stop the people from merely voting Bird and his cronies back into power during the next election?
